  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  SECOND SEMESTER B.TECH. EXAMINATIONS - MAY/JUNE 2023  
  SUBJECT: PHY 1071-PHY/ PHY 1071-B/ PHY 1051-B - ENGINEERING PHYSICS  
  ENGINEERING PHYSICS [PHY 1071-PHY]  
  Marks: 50                                                                                 Duration: 180 mins.  
  A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1A)          Explain why do we need coherent light source in Young's double slit experiment? Derive  
  an expression for linear positions of bright and dark fringes in double slit interference (5)  
  pattern.  
  
  1B)          A screen is placed 50.0 cm from a single slit, which is illuminated with light of  
  wavelength 690 nm. If the distance between the first and third minima in the diffraction (3)  
  pattern is 3.00 mm, what is the width of the slit?  
  
  1C)          How do you justify that the quantum harmonic oscillator never be at rest?  
  (2)  
  
  2A)          Explain the following terms with reference to lasers:  
  i) Spontaneous emission                                                                         (5)  
  ii) Stimulated emission  
  
  2B)          A step index optical fiber 63.5 m in core-diameter has a core of refractive index 1.53  
  and a cladding of index 1.39. Determine (a) the numerical aperture for the fiber, (b) the  
  critical angle for core-cladding interface, (c) the acceptance cone half-angle (the             (3)  
  maximum entrance angle).  
  
  2C)  
  
  (2)  
  
  
  3A)          (i) What is the Compton effect? (ii) Sketch the graph of scattered X-ray intensity versus  
  $$wavelength for scattered X-ray angle at \theta  = 0˚, \theta  = 45˚ and \theta  = 135˚. (iii) Derive an     (5)$$  
  expression for Compton shift.  
  
  3B)          A FM radio transmitter operates at a frequency of 98.3 MHz, having a power output of  
  134 kW. Calculate the number of photons per second emitted by the transmitter. Also,            (3)  
  calculate the total energy (in eV) transmitted by FM radio in 10 seconds.  
  
  3C)          The temperature of two perfect blackbodies, A and B, are 400 K and 200 K,                       (2)  
  respectively. If the surface area of A is twice that of B, then determine the ratio of total  
  power radiated by A to that of B.

  4A)             Solve the Schrodinger equation and derive an expression for the normalized wave  
  function for a particle of mass m in an infinite one-dimensional potential well [box] of  
  width L and potential zero inside the well. Sketch wave functions for the allowed  
  quantum states n = 1 and n = 4 for the potential-energy well given in the figure below.  
  
  
  (5)  
  
  
  4B)             An electron trapped in an infinite potential well of width 15 nm absorbs a photon of  
  frequency 4.86×1012 Hz and jumps from an even-numbered excited state to the next            (3)  
  higher even-number excited state. Find the two excited states.  
  
  4C)             What are intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors? Can you explain the different types of  
  extrinsic semiconductors with suitable examples?                                            (2)  
  
  5A)             Derive an expression for density-of-states function for an electron in metals.  
  (5)  
  
  5B)             The cesium iodide (CsI) molecule has an atomic separation of 0.127 nm. (a) Determine  
  the energy of the second excited rotational state, with J = 2. (b) Find the frequency of the  
  photon absorbed in the J = 1 to J = 2 transition. The atomic masses of cesium and iodine (3)  
  $$are 132.9u and 126.9u respectively. (Given: 1u = 1.66 10-27 kg.)$$  
  
  5C)             What is quantum confinement and how does it affect the properties of materials at the  
  nanoscale?                                                                                  (2)
